question: In covering a distance of 156 km, Abhay takes 5 hours more than Sameer. If Abhay doubles his speed, then he would take 8 hours less than Sameer. Abhay's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

If Abhay doubles his speed, his time is halved (from T to T/2).

Total difference in Abhay's time = 5 hours (more) + 8 hours (less) = 13 hours.

So, T − T/2 = 13 ⇒ T/2 = 13 ⇒ T = 26 hours.

Abhay's speed = Distance ÷ Time = 156 ÷ 26 = 6 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 156 km

Abhay initially takes 5 hours more than Sameer.

When Abhay doubles his speed, he takes 8 hours less than Sameer.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 Distance = 156 km

**Calculations:**

Let Sameer's time be t hours.

⇒ Abhay's original time (T) = t + 5 (Equation 1)

When Abhay doubles his speed, his new time becomes half, i.e., T/2.

⇒ Abhay's new time (T/2) = t − 8 (Equation 2)

Subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ T − T/2 = (t + 5) − (t − 8)

⇒ T/2 = 13

⇒ T = 26 hours

Now, substitute the time into the speed formula:

⇒ Abhay's Speed = Total Distance ÷ Original Time

⇒ Abhay's Speed = 156 ÷ 26

⇒ Abhay's Speed = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Speed and Time

For a constant distance, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed is multiplied by a factor x, the time taken is divided by x.

Average Speed

When a distance is covered in parts, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
